bar.codeHint: Which QR version, error correction and module size
bar.startAgainBody: Every setting goes back to how it started. The design you have now is lost.
view.canvas: The tile. Drag to turn it, scroll to zoom.
view.scanCanvas: The code as a reader sees it
view.scanNote: Point a phone at this. If it reads here, it will read off the print — same modules, same quiet zone, same cleared middle.
view.look: Which way to look at it
content.shortenHint: Writes the scheme and domain in capitals, which a QR code packs into fewer modules, so they come out bigger. The path is left alone, because a path is case-sensitive.
content.secret: The password goes into the code itself. Anyone who scans it, or who gets the file, has it.
content.correctionHint: How much of the code can be damaged, dirty or covered and still read. More correction means more modules, so each one comes out smaller.
content.level.L: Survives about 7% damage. The fewest modules.
content.level.M: Survives about 15%. What most codes use.
content.level.Q: Survives about 25%. Worth it with a logo in the middle.
content.level.H: Survives about 30%. For a big logo, or a code that will get knocked about.
content.versionHint: How many modules across the code is. Left on its own it takes the smallest that fits, which makes each module as big as it can be.
content.holds: Holding {used} of {capacity} {mode} characters, in version {version} at {modules} × {modules} modules.
content.couldBeSmaller: Version {version} would hold this, with bigger modules.
content.needUrl: Type an address to put in the code.
content.needText: Type the text to put in the code.
content.needSsid: Type the name of the network.
content.needContact: Fill in at least one thing about the contact.
shape.sizeByHint: Either you choose how big one module is and the tile follows, or you choose the tile and the modules follow.
shape.moduleHint: A module under about 1 mm is hard for a printer to draw and hard for a phone to read.
shape.plateHint: The border counts; the keyring tab doesn't.
shape.quietHint: The clear margin round the code. A reader needs it to find where the code starts; the standard asks for four modules of it.
shape.borderOn: A raised frame round the code
shape.borderHint: A frame in its own colour, outside the quiet zone, which also gives the tile an edge to hold.
shape.tabPositionHint: Where the loop sits along its edge: the middle at 0, either end at ±100. It stops short of the rounded corners.
shape.tabNote: The loop stands proud of the edge and is as thick as the tile, so the two are one piece.
style.raisedHint: The dark modules stand above the tile. Prints in one colour if you like; a scanner then reads the shadows, so it wants good light.
style.flushHint: The dark modules and the light around them are the same height, so the top is smooth and the colours do the work. Needs two filaments.
style.inlayHint: How thick the two-colour layer on top of the tile is. About 0.6 mm is plenty to cover.
style.fillHint: How much of its cell each module fills. Under 100% leaves a gap between neighbours; over 100% closes it up.
style.raisedNote: Printed in one colour this still scans in good light, but two colours is what a phone likes.
style.flushNote: The top comes out smooth: swap filament at the layer where the code starts, or let a multi-material printer do it.
style.bodyHint: The shape every dark module takes. Rounded and bevelled smooth where a module stands free, so a run of them reads as one; bars and columns join a run outright. The plainer the shape, the easier the read — a dot fills less of its cell, so keep the modules big.
style.eyesHint: The big squares in the corners are what a reader finds first, so they are drawn as one piece and can be styled apart from the rest. On Match they take the shape that goes with the modules.
style.reliefHint: What the tops of the raised modules do. Three shape each module; four stand them at different heights across the code. All of them taper upwards or stay flat, so none needs supports.
style.reliefFlush: A flush code has nothing standing up to shape: the relief shows once you go back to raised modules.
colour.filamentsHint: One filament per colour. Two parts of the same colour print in the same one, so a border in the code's colour costs nothing extra.
colour.caption: Caption
colour.contrastHint: A reader tells the modules from the tile by how light they are, not by hue. Dark on light, or light on dark, with plenty between them.
colour.ratioPoor: too little: a phone will struggle
extras.caption: Caption
extras.captionHint: Words under or over the code, raised in their own colour, for what the code is: a name, a room, a machine.
extras.patchHint: Clears the modules in the middle for a logo. Error correction covers what is cleared, up to a point — the check panel says how much was used up.
extras.patchAcrossHint: How many modules wide the patch is. Every module it touches is cleared, so the logo never sits half on one.
extras.logoNote: An SVG of outlines — paths, rectangles, circles, polygons. Text has to be turned into outlines first, and a bitmap can't be printed.
check.title: Before you print
check.hint: What would stop this scanning, or stop it printing cleanly.
check.nothingHint: Fill in what the code should say.
check.scanIt: Switch to “Scan it” and read it with a phone before you print it.
check.moduleFineWhy: Wide enough for a {nozzle} mm nozzle to draw cleanly and for a phone to resolve.
check.quietFineWhy: Four modules of clear margin, which is what the standard asks for.
check.contrastFineWhy: The two filaments are far enough apart in lightness for a reader to tell them apart.
check.wholeCodeWhy: Nothing is covered, so the whole of level {level}'s {recovery}% is spare.
check.moduleTinyFix: That is about the width of a nozzle: the modules will run together. Make the module bigger, or use less error correction so there are fewer of them.
check.moduleSmallFix: It may read, but 1.2 mm or more is safer in print. Make the tile bigger or shorten what the code says.
check.noQuietZoneFix: A reader needs clear space round a code to find it. Set the margin back to compact at least, or leave the tile's own colour round it.
check.shortQuietZoneFix: The standard asks for four. Two usually works on a clean tile; one phone in ten will take longer.
check.sameColourRaisedFix: A raised code in a single colour reads by shadow alone, so it wants side light. Give the code its own filament if you can.
check.sameColourFlush: Flush, and both colours the same
check.sameColourFlushFix: Nothing stands up and nothing is darker, so there is nothing to read. Change the code's colour, or go back to raised modules.
check.lowContrastFix: Take the code darker or the tile lighter. Hue doesn't help a reader; lightness does.
check.patchTooBig: The patch covers {share}% of the modules
check.patchTooBigFix: Level {level} can't make that up. Make the patch smaller, or go up to Q or H.
check.patchCovers: The patch covers {share}% of the modules
check.patchCoversFix: Level {level} can rebuild that, but there is less left over for dirt and wear.
check.thinModulesFix: A fill under 85% on modules this small leaves very little to print. Raise the fill, or make the modules bigger.
check.biggerThanBedFix: That is wider than most printers' beds. Make the module smaller, or shorten what the code says.
check.tallModules: Modules are taller than they are wide
check.tallModulesFix: Tall thin pillars print poorly and cast shadows a reader may take for modules. Bring the height down.
check.bigVersionFix: That many modules only reads if it is printed big. Keep an eye on the module size.
check.biggerThanNeededFix: Letting the version follow what fits would make every module bigger, which prints and scans better.
check.captionShrunk: The caption was set {percent}% of the size asked for
check.captionShrunkFix: It was too long for the tile. Shorten it, or make the capital height smaller yourself.
check.captionEmpty: Nothing to set in the caption
check.captionEmptyFix: The typeface has none of those characters as outlines. Try another typeface.
check.captionNoFontFix: Thingport couldn't hand over a typeface, so the words are left off the model. Try again, or clear the caption.
part.caption: Caption
error.empty: There's nothing to put in the code yet.
error.tooMuch: That's more than any QR code holds. Shorten it, or use less error correction.
error.wontFitVersion: That won't fit in version {version}. Version {needed} is the smallest that holds it.
file.3mfNote: For Bambu Studio, Orca and PrusaSlicer
file.stlNote: The raised shape, for anything that reads nothing else
file.pngNote: Black on white, for printing or sharing
file.projectNote: Every setting, to open here again
file.notesNote: The sizes, the filaments and the warnings, as text
save.title: Save to Thingport
save.name: QR code — {name}
save.where: Saved as a 3MF with a part per filament, a picture of the tile and one of the code itself.
save.secret: The Wi-Fi password is in the file. Anyone who can open the model can read it.
notes.code: QR version {version} ({modules} × {modules} modules), error correction {level} ({recovery}%), mask {mask}.
notes.raised: The code stands above the tile: print it flat, code side up.
notes.flush: The code is flush with the tile: the top layer is two colours at one height.
notes.madeWith: Made with Thingport's QR code generator {version}.
toast.stillWorking: Still working it out — one moment.
toast.wontBuildYet: That won't build yet. Check the settings.
toast.logoTooBig: That SVG is too big. Keep it under 2 MB.
toast.logoPartly: {count} thing(s) in that file aren't outlines and were left out.
toast.projectFailed: That isn't a design this tool wrote.
toast.noWebgl: This browser has no 3D, so the flat view is all there is.
